thread:
maya-docs: Hey all — I've opened a docs PR with compact cross-language streaming examples + a short 'resume token' pattern. Link: <https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-docs/pull/3821|#3821>
sam-devex: Nice. Can you summarize what changed?
maya-docs: Main changes: 1) Python example for resume tokens + KV-prefix cache, 2) TS example showing AbortSignal + exponential backoff for stream reconnect, 3) Go pattern that uses a channel + context cancellation for consuming stream tokens. Kept each snippet tiny (~12-18 LOC).
raj-eng: Quick skim: The Go example uses a single goroutine per stream; is that ok for high-concurrency customers?
maya-docs: Good question — I added a note that the pattern is intended for per-request handling; recommend worker pools for high concurrency and link to runtime batching guide.
olivia-qa: CI flagged a docs link check failure for the runtime batching doc in the PR. ci-bot: build failed — dead link at docs/perf/batching.md (404).
maya-docs: Argh. I updated an internal path but missed the public doc. I'll fix the link in the PR now.
sam-devex: Also, the TS example references AbortSignal.timeout which is Node 18+ only. We should either polyfill or mention Node minimum.
maya-docs: Good catch — added a small note: "Node >=18 / browser native AbortController required", and included a tiny fallback snippet using setTimeout + controller.abort().
raj-eng: For the resume token flow: what's the expected semantics? Are tokens opaque server-side or should we show how to store them client-side?
maya-docs: Docs show client stores opaque resume_token and sends it as "resume_token" metadata in the next request. Python snippet demonstrates persisting to Redis KV and reusing prefix cache.
alex-product: Product note: callers often ask about dedup when resuming — maybe add a sentence that server-side dedup is recommended and to keep messages idempotent where possible.
maya-docs: Added a one-liner on dedup and a link to idempotency recommendations.
olivia-qa: CI re-run? ci-bot: re-run requested by @maya-docs
ci-bot: build started — running linkcheck, md-lint, snippet-tests.
ci-bot: snippet-tests: running python/ts/go examples in sandbox (sanity checks)
ci-bot: linkcheck: all links OK now.
ci-bot: snippet-tests: python example passed, ts example passed, go example failed — data race detected in example harness (goroutine leak).
raj-eng: I expected that — my bad, the example didn't cancel the stream consumer in error paths. Quick fix: ensure ctx.Done() is watched and close the out channel in defer.
maya-docs: Pushed small fix to PR, see commit message "close out chan on ctx.Done()".
ci-bot: re-run requested by @raj-eng
ci-bot: snippet-tests: go example passed. All checks green.
sam-devex: LGTM from docs side. A few tiny wording nits (avoid 'magic token') — left inline comments on PR.
olivia-qa: From QA: added an extra test case verifying resume after partial stream — passes with the new examples.
alex-product: Approved from PM side, let's schedule the merge after 24h in case any other folks want to review.
maya-docs: Sounds good. I'll squash the commits and mark the PR ready to merge. Thanks everyone :tada:
sam-devex: Nice job. Can we follow up with a short sample repo that wires Python + Redis for the resume token example? Might be handy for users.
maya-docs: Added a TODO in the PR to track a sample repo (GH issue link in PR).
raj-eng: One last note for runtime: added comment about adjusting kv_cache_ttl when using resume tokens so old prefixes don't get evicted too quickly.
maya-docs: Added that note under "Operational considerations".
ci-bot: PR #3821 — all checks passed. Ready to merge in 24h if no objections.
